title: The Complete Sri Lanka Travel Guide
subtitle: How the island divides, how to choose between the ten destinations, how to plan around the two monsoons and the trains, and what two weeks can realistically hold.
summary: Sri Lanka packs ancient kingdoms, tea hills, safaris and beaches into a small island. This guide covers how the regions divide, how to choose between the ten destinations, how to travel, when to go, what it costs and three routes that work.

faq.q: Should I hire a driver or use public transport?
faq.a: A car with a driver is the easiest and most flexible, and it is affordable. Trains are the best experience for the hill country. Buses are cheap but crowded.
The south and west from December to March, and the east from April to September. The cultural triangle and hills are good most of the year.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book the Ella train?
faq.a: Reserved seats on the Kandy–Ella line sell out weeks ahead in season. Book early or use a second-class ticket.

faq.q: Is Sri Lanka easy for first-timers to Asia?
faq.a: Yes. English is widely understood, people are friendly, and distances are short.

sections.title: How Sri Lanka divides
body: Sri Lanka is about 435 km from north to south, and for a visitor it falls into five zones.
**The west and Colombo.** [[colombo|Colombo]] is the gateway city, with an international airport 35 km north.
**The Cultural Triangle.** [[sigiriya|Sigiriya]], [[anuradhapura|Anuradhapura]] and [[polonnaruwa|Polonnaruwa]] hold the ancient kingdoms, with [[kandy|Kandy]] at the southern edge.
**The hill country.** [[nuwara-eliya|Nuwara Eliya]] and [[ella|Ella]] are cool, green and famous for tea and trains.
**The south.** [[galle|Galle]], [[mirissa|Mirissa]] and [[yala|Yala]] offer beaches, whales and wildlife.
sections.note: The practical route is a loop: Colombo, the Cultural Triangle, Kandy, the hills and the south coast.

list.title: If you have one week
list.text: [[sigiriya|Sigiriya]], [[kandy|Kandy]] and [[ella|Ella]], with a train ride between the last two.

list.title: If you love wildlife
list.text: [[yala|Yala]] for leopards, Minneriya near [[polonnaruwa|Polonnaruwa]] for elephants, and [[mirissa|Mirissa]] for whales.

list.title: If you love hiking and scenery
If you love beaches
list.text: [[mirissa|Mirissa]] and the south coast, best from December to March.

list.title: If you love city life
list.text: [[colombo|Colombo]] for food and shopping, [[galle|Galle]] for atmosphere and [[kandy|Kandy]] for culture.

sections.title: Getting around
body: Roads are slow and winding, so distances that look short on a map can take hours.
**Car with driver.** Popular, comfortable and affordable. Your driver often knows the best stops.
**Trains.** The Kandy–Ella line is a highlight. Reserve seats early.
**Buses.** Very cheap and frequent, but crowded and fast.
**Tuk-tuks.** For short hops. Use PickMe or agree fares.
sections.note: The expressways from Colombo to Galle and Matara save hours on the south coast.

sections.title: When to go
body: Sri Lanka's two monsoons decide the best place to be.
December to March: the south-west coast, hills and Yala are dry and sunny. This is the peak season.
April to May: hot and humid, with thunderstorms. A quiet time.
June to September: the south-west coast is rough and wet, but the Cultural Triangle, Kandy and the east coast are dry. Minneriya elephant gatherings peak.
October and November: heavy rain nearly everywhere.
sections.note: Whales off [[mirissa|Mirissa]] are best seen from December to April.

sections.title: Money, costs and safety
body: Sri Lanka is good value. A local meal costs US$2–6, a mid-range hotel US$40–90, and a driver with car US$50–90 per day.
Entrance fees to major sites such as Sigiriya are charged in US dollars and are high for foreigners.
Beware of scams and inflated prices from touts. Use reputable operators for safaris and whale watching.
Take care in the sea, since currents are strong.

list.title: One week: culture and hills
list.text: Two nights near [[sigiriya|Sigiriya]], two in [[kandy|Kandy]], and three in [[ella|Ella]].
list.tip: Take the train from Kandy to Ella.

list.title: Two weeks: the classic
list.text: The itinerary on the country page, covering all ten destinations from [[colombo|Colombo]] to [[galle|Galle]].
list.tip: Skip Anuradhapura if you are short of time.
